scope: Item 20 compact grouped COUNT/SUM/AVG storage after direct-Parquet Q33 memory refusal

reproduction.result: Old representation refuses the unchanged budget; compact representation passes every output row.

frozen_mechanism: Use existing leased DensePages for a compact high-cardinality grouped COUNT/SUM/AVG representation below every public interface. Keep native key interning, result ordering, numeric updates and source ownership contracts.
admission: Grouped specifications containing only COUNT and non-decimal SUM/AVG may migrate once their generic per-group state exceeds 1 MiB. Smaller and other aggregate families retain existing representation. Migrate only completed earlier states, reserve migration overlap, then release generic storage. This is a storage representation threshold, not a performance cutoff.
storage: Eight bytes per COUNT and count plus the existing NumericAggregateSum per SUM/AVG, in independently leased pages. Retain stable group ordinals, charged page metadata, cancellation, deterministic denial and drop cleanup.
semantic_gate: Preserve complete values, NULL/empty/filter behavior, per-measure and per-row arithmetic/error order, signed zero, compensated integer totals, nonfinite refusal and count-overflow state. Keep adjacent completed-update reuse where admitted. No limit changes or fallback.

retention_decision.performance_rule: Compare once against 15.180311963 engine seconds with no percentage gain floor. Preserve every observation and flag. Do not describe the required memory correction as an optimization unless complete-cohort gain is observed.

held_out_correctness.scope: Complete counts, additive values, alias chains, filtered input, all-NULL groups, mixed widths, 32779 unique groups and empty groups. Per-measure filters and lifetime also use the public regression.

correctness: Regression first: a bounded many-group, multi-measure workload must fail the old representation under a fixed small memory budget and pass after the correction.

Fresh independent complete results across public interfaces, source readback and ownership checks.
